Definition: , including feminine οὐδεμία, and neuter οὐδέν from G3761 and G1520; not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing:--any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought.
BiblicalUsage: No one, or nothing, is the strongest negative pronoun. Paul thanks God that he baptized none of the Corinthians, and John says God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe no one is the word that clears the room: no one can come to the Father except by Jesus, and no darkness at all is in God.
